
Load `tidyverse` package using the `library` function.

```{r}
# Load tidyverse
library(tidyverse)
```


Load our data.

```{r}
# Load the data
d_blomkvist <- read_csv("../../data/blomkvist.csv")

# Remove missing category for smoker and missing values for rt
d_blomkvist <- drop_na(d_blomkvist, smoker, rt_hand_d)
```

We will create a plot first and then change the colour of the colour aesthetic.

```{r}
plot_rt <- ggplot(d_blomkvist, aes(x = rt_hand_d, y = rt_hand_nd, colour = meds_cat)) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
```



 Change colour values manually
- Colour names: [link](http://sape.inf.usi.ch/quick-reference/ggplot2/colour)



Changing the colour scheme.
You can define colours yourself but often it is easier to use functions that provide colour schemes.

Here are some example.

The first one is designed for people that struggle to distinguish colours and do a good job when printed on a grey scale.

```{r eval = FALSE}
install.packages("ggthemes")
```


```{r}
library(ggthemes)
```


```{r}
plot_rt + scale_colour_colorblind() # `ggthemes` package
plot_rt + scale_color_wsj() # `ggthemes` package
plot_rt + scale_colour_viridis_d()
```

Select your favorite and add the plot to `rt_plot`

```{r}
rt_plot <- rt_plot + scale_colour_---()
```
